svg.title: Prompt caching mechanics by provider, November 2026
svg.desc: A comparison grid with three provider columns, OpenAI, Anthropic and Gemini, and six rows. How it is turned on: OpenAI caches automatically with no code; Anthropic needs cache_control, either top-level for automatic caching or per block; Gemini has implicit caching on by default and explicit caching through a cache object. Breakpoints: OpenAI chooses implicit breakpoints, and GPT-5.6 and later add explicit breakpoints with up to four cache writes; Anthropic allows up to four breakpoints per request and automatic caching uses one slot; Gemini implicit caching chooses for you and an explicit cache covers the whole object. Lifetime: OpenAI 30 minutes by default or 12 hours on GPT-5.6 and later; Anthropic 5 minutes refreshed on use, or 1 hour; Gemini explicit caches live for the TTL you set, 1 hour by default. Minimum prefix: OpenAI 1,024 tokens on GPT-5.6 and later, varying on older models; Anthropic 512 to 4,096 tokens depending on the model; Gemini 2,048 to 4,096 tokens depending on the model. Seen in usage as: OpenAI cached_tokens and cache_write_tokens; Anthropic cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens; Gemini cachedContentTokenCount in usageMetadata. Relative cost: OpenAI on GPT-5.6 and later bills writes above the input price and reads far below it; Anthropic bills writes above the input price and reads at a small fraction; Gemini discounts hits, and explicit caches add storage cost per hour.

g.text: reads a small fraction of it
Same idea everywhere (reuse an identical prefix), different switches, lifetimes and minimums. Check the docs per model.
